safety.name: General laboratory rules
safety.intro: Baseline conduct that applies to everyone, every day, in every part of the laboratory.

items: Wear a buttoned lab coat, closed footwear and gloves appropriate to the task.
Know where the fire extinguisher, first-aid box, eye-wash and exits are before you start work.
Label everything you prepare: contents, concentration, date, your name.
Wash hands on entering and leaving, and after removing gloves.
Enter instrument use in log books; report every fault, however small.
Eat, drink, chew or store food anywhere in the laboratory — including the refrigerator.
Mouth-pipette anything, ever.
Work alone on hazardous procedures outside working hours.
Wear gloves on door handles, phones, or shared keyboards.
Leave flames, hot plates or water baths running unattended.

safety.name: Molecular biology laboratory
safety.intro: The molecular lab combines chemical, electrical and UV hazards with contamination-sensitive work.

items: Treat the gel area, transilluminator, gel tanks and combs as permanently EtBr-contaminated.
Double nitrile gloves when handling stained gels; change outer gloves before touching anything else.
Keep a dedicated EtBr waste container for gels and tips; never bin or drain them.
Wipe the transilluminator and bench with damp tissue then 70% ethanol after every session.
Unpolymerised acrylamide is a neurotoxin — weigh powder only in the hood; prefer ready solutions.
TEMED is flammable and corrosive: open only in a ventilated spot, cap immediately.
Polymerised gel is safer but edges may hold unpolymerised residue — gloves throughout.
Connect leads before switching on; switch off and unplug before opening any tank.
Keep bench and hands dry; buffer conducts.
Damaged leads or cracked tanks go for repair, not one more run.
Face shield, long sleeves and gloves at the transilluminator — UV burns skin and cornea in minutes.
Keep gel exposure short; use LOW intensity when cutting bands.
Pre-PCR and post-PCR areas, pipettes and racks stay separate; amplified DNA never travels back.
Filter tips for all PCR setup; gloves changed after handling products.

safety.name: Laminar air flow & aseptic work
safety.intro: The cabinet protects your cultures; discipline protects you.

items: UV lamp on for 15–20 min with the shutter closed — and nobody working near the open front.
Never enter or reach into the cabinet while the UV lamp is on.
Switch UV off, blower on for 10–15 min before starting work.
Swab the surface and your gloved hands with 70% ethanol.
Work at least 15 cm inside the front edge; keep arms low and movements slow.
Keep the spirit lamp flame small; 70% ethanol and flames sit apart — ethanol fires in cabinets are common accidents.
Do not block the rear/bottom grilles with bottles or notebooks.
This cabinet protects the work, not you — it is not a biosafety cabinet for human pathogens.
Remove everything; the cabinet is not a storage shelf.
Swab the surface, switch off blower and light, close the shutter.
If ethanol catches fire: cover with the metal lid or damp cloth — never pour water on burning ethanol near electrics.

safety.name: Handling pathogens & cultures
safety.intro: Plant pathogens rarely harm people, but they can devastate crops — containment protects the crop in the field, and good technique protects your own lungs from spore-laden air.

items: Keep plates taped or parafilmed once colonies grow; open sporulating cultures only in the laminar flow.
Heavy sporulators (Aspergillus, Penicillium contaminants) can trigger allergy — avoid sniffing plates.
Label every culture with code, organism, date; maintain the culture register.
Inoculated plants stay in the designated glasshouse/net-house; never carry pathogens out on clothing or tools.
All used cultures, spent plates and inoculated material are autoclaved (121 °C, 30 min minimum) before washing or disposal.
Autoclave waste in autoclavable bags, loosely closed so steam penetrates.
Benches wiped with 70% ethanol (or 1% hypochlorite for spills) after culture work.
Contaminated glassware soaks in disinfectant before it joins general washing.
Cover the spill with paper towels; pour 1% sodium hypochlorite from the edges inward.
Leave 15–20 minutes contact time, then wipe up with gloves into an autoclave bag.
Swab the area again with disinfectant; wash hands thoroughly.

safety.name: Chemical handling & storage
safety.intro: Most chemical accidents are weighing, transferring and mixing errors — slow down at those steps.

items: Check the label and the Chemicals tab hazard badge; for HIGH-hazard chemicals read the SDS first.
Weigh hazardous powders (acrylamide, PCNB, dichromate, azide) in the hood or with the balance draught shield closed, mask on.
Carry acid/alkali bottles with two hands or in a bottle carrier, never by the neck.
Always add acid to water, never water to acid.
Add KOH/NaOH pellets to water slowly with stirring — the solution gets hot.
Never mix hypochlorite (bleach) with acids — chlorine gas evolves.
Sodium azide never meets acids or metal plumbing — explosive/toxic products.

Follow the refrigerator notice: CI, 0.5 M EDTA, 1 M Tris-HCl, 5 M NaCl and CTAB stay at room temperature; isopropanol and absolute alcohol are chilled in the deep freezer before use, not stored in the fridge.
Flammables (alcohols, TEMED) away from hot plates, flames and direct sun.
Oxidisers (nitrates, dichromate) shelved apart from organic solvents and combustibles.
Keep containers closed; hygroscopic salts (CaCl₂, FeCl₃, ZnCl₂) cake and corrode when left open.

safety.name: Chemical spill
safety.intro: Small bench spills you can handle; large or unknown spills you evacuate and report.

blocks.h: Small spill (a few mL, known chemical)
items: Alert people nearby; put on gloves and, for volatile chemicals, work fast or ventilate.
Contain with paper towels from the edges inward.
Acids: neutralise cautiously with sodium bicarbonate before wiping. Alkalis: dilute with plenty of water while wiping.
Collect residues into a labelled waste container — not the sink.
Wash the area with water and detergent; wash hands.
Wear double gloves; absorb with paper towels.
Wash the surface repeatedly with detergent and water (decontamination solutions if available).
All towels and gloves go to EtBr solid waste.

blocks.h: Large spill / strong acid / unknown / fuming
items: Do not attempt cleanup. Warn everyone, leave the room, close the door.
Cut power to the area if safely possible.
Inform the laboratory in-charge immediately; ventilate before re-entry is approved.

safety.name: Chemical on skin or in eyes
safety.intro: Speed matters more than technique — water, immediately, and lots of it.

items: Remove contaminated gloves/clothing immediately.
Flush the area under running water for at least 15 minutes.
Do NOT apply neutralising chemicals to skin — no bicarbonate on acid burns, no vinegar on alkali burns; only water.
For phenol/lactophenol contact: flood with water, then wipe with glycerol or PEG if available; seek medical help.
Seek medical attention for anything beyond trivial contact; carry the chemical's name/SDS.
Go to the eye-wash or any gentle running water source instantly.
Hold the eyelids open and irrigate for a full 15 minutes, rolling the eye.
Remove contact lenses if easily possible while flushing.
Always get medical attention afterwards, even if the eye feels normal — alkali damage evolves over hours.
Move to fresh air at once; loosen tight clothing.
If breathing difficulty persists, seek medical help immediately; note which chemical was involved.

safety.name: Fire
safety.intro: Small, contained, and you trained on the extinguisher — fight it. Anything more — evacuate.

items: Raise the alarm — shout, alert everyone in the lab.
Cut power to the affected equipment/bench if the switch is safely reachable.
Small bench fire: smother with a fire blanket/damp cloth or use the extinguisher (aim at the base, sweep).
Burning ethanol/solvent: smother — never water.
Clothing on fire: STOP–DROP–ROLL; wrap the person in a lab coat or blanket.

blocks.h: If it is not immediately controlled
items: Evacuate; close (do not lock) doors behind you.
Do not use lifts; assemble away from the building and account for everyone.
Call the fire service and inform the department office; re-enter only when declared safe.
Know your extinguisher location and type before you ever need it.
Flammables never sit beside hot plates or open flames.
Overloaded sockets and frayed cords are reported, not tolerated.

safety.name: Electric shock & equipment accidents
safety.intro: Electricity plus wet benches is the lab's most underrated danger.

items: Do NOT touch the person while they are in contact with the source.
Cut power at the switch/mains, or separate them from the source using dry non-conductive material (wooden rod, rubber).
Once clear: check responsiveness and breathing; call for medical help.
If not breathing, start CPR if trained; continue until help arrives.
All shocks, however brief, are reported — cardiac effects can be delayed.
Sparking, smoking or burning-smell equipment: switch off at the mains, unplug if safe, do not reuse until inspected.
Centrifuge making abnormal noise: stop it, let the rotor halt fully, never open early.
Broken UV lamp or transilluminator glass: switch off, gloves for cleanup, sharps container for the glass.
Let small cuts bleed briefly under running water, then antiseptic and dressing from the first-aid box.
Deep cuts: apply firm pressure with a clean pad, elevate, seek medical attention.
Never pick broken glass with fingers — brush and dustpan, into the sharps/glass container.
